items.title: Live: US Navy begins blockade of Hormuz, Trump claims Iran 'very badly' wants deal
items.description: The US Navy is expected to begin its blockade of the Strait of Hormuz after Trump warned he would do so following failed peace talks with Iran. Follow live.

items.title: Trump's defamation lawsuit against Wall Street Journal over Epstein story dismissed
items.description: The case related to a Wall Street Journal article that described a sexually suggestive letter that the newspaper said was included in a 2003 album compiled for Epstein’s 50th birthday.

items.title: 'Should have done this earlier': Former CIA boss backs Trump's blockade
items.description: Donald Trump's looming blockade of the Strait of Hormuz will likely lead to confrontation warns a former 4-star general and former head of the CIA.

items.title: Trump's strait blockade has two immediate implications for the world and China
items.description: Donald Trump's planned United States naval blockade of Iranian vessels in the Strait of Hormuz reveals the president once again playing loose with the fortunes of financial markets and the global economy as he struggles to find a way out of the war that he and Israel started.

items.title: Australia's LNG exporters will face a tougher future, new report says
items.description: The long-term outlook for Australia's liquefied natural gas exports is structurally constrained by declining demand, and the current war in the Middle East may hasten that shift away from gas, a new report claims.

items.title: The US will cut off the Strait of Hormuz. Here's what the blockade means
items.description: US president Donald Trump has ordered his nation's military to cut off all Iranian ports from maritime traffic passing through the Strait of Hormuz, one of the world's most vital shipping routes.

items.title: Booking.com customers involved in possible data and security breach
items.description: Some Booking.com customers are being warned their personal information may have been accessed by unauthorised third parties, prompting fresh concerns about the security of travellers' data.

items.title: Social media checks for all visa applicants under Angus Taylor plan
items.description: Social media screening would be introduced for all visa applicants under an immigration policy to be revealed by Opposition leader Angus Taylor.

items.title: Albanese names new defence force chief
items.description: Vice Admiral Mark Hammond, who has spent 40 years in the navy, will replace current defence force chief David Johnston when he retires in July.

items.title: Coachella boasted big-name artists — the special guests were maybe even bigger
items.description: The world's most talked-about music festival took place over the weekend, boasting a bevy of unexpected highlights.

items.title: Federal MPs urged not to speak out about looming Ben Roberts-Smith trial
items.description: A federal MP and former commando has urged colleagues from across the aisle to refrain from speaking out about the arrest of accused war criminal Ben Roberts-Smith.

items.title: How did a 3km hike go so wrong? Retracing Celine Cremer's final steps
items.description: Belgian backpacker Celine Cremer was on the trip of a lifetime, but on a hike in Tasmania she left the trail and was never seen again. It took a private investigator, a YouTuber, loved ones and an army of volunteers to find answers.

items.title: Student vaccinated without consent prompts council concern
items.description: A Tasmanian mayor is calling on the state government to take on responsibility for running school immunisation programs, after a student was vaccinated without caregiver consent.

items.title: Growers could 'pull the pin' as fuel costs soar
items.description: As fuel prices remain high amid the war in the Middle East, growers and fishers are among those having to make tough decisions to remain viable.

items.title: Euphoria season 3 cast on past, present and future of hit show
items.description: Season 3 of Euphoria has premiered today as members of the cast reflect on where the show has been and where it's going.

items.title: Australia's best inventor you've never heard of
items.description: Solar power is forecast to overtake coal as the world's biggest source of electricity next year, and its growth shows no signs of slowing down. Behind its success is a little-known Australian inventor.

items.title: Reptile remains believed to be a crocodile found dumped on side of road
items.description: Reptile remains — which are believed to be from a crocodile — have been collected by authorities after they were found dumped on the side of an Adelaide road.

items.title: These five soup recipes are comfort in a bowl
items.description: Looking for new soup recipes as the weather cools? From minestrone to hot and sour dumplings, we have you covered.

items.title: Butters sent to Tribunal over 'abusive and insulting' umpire sledge
items.description: Port Adelaide star Zak Butters will front the AFL Tribunal over an exchange with umpire Nick Foot.

items.title: Backyard astronomer who helped to discover 100 distant planets awarded medal
items.description: From a backyard observatory in regional Victoria, Gippsland astronomer Chris Stockdale spends his nights helping confirm distant planets by tracking tiny changes in starlight that reveal new worlds beyond our solar system.

items.title: World-famous Horizontal Falls to allow more tourists, with cultural focus
items.description: Tourism operators, the state government and traditional owners strike an agreement about the future of tourism at the famed Horizontal Falls in WA's Kimberley.

items.title: Memorial for women allegedly killed by men removed from Melbourne laneway
items.description: The founder of Australian Femicide Watch says she is heartbroken over the removal of the She Matters mural in Hosier Lane dedicated to more than 200 women who have died since January 2025.

items.title: Canada has flipped the script on child care. Could Australia copy?
items.description: Australia definitely won't nationalise child care, even though the data suggests there's a strong case. Perhaps a more feasible idea would be to copy what Canada has done.

items.title: 'Absolute garbage': NSW police minister hits back at mayor's resourcing claims
items.description: A $1.8 million plaza closed by council has become a flashpoint in a war of words over police resources in Sydney's west.

items.title: One Nation approaches independent MPs as it makes the case to be SA's opposition
items.description: One Nation SA leader Cory Bernardi has approached independent MPs to make the case for his party — instead of the Liberals — to be recognised as the state's official opposition.
